scenarios.title: The Tunnel
scenarios.text: In the tunnel before kick-off, the opposition captain refuses to shake his hand. The cameras are right there.

choices.label: Smile and keep the hand out
choices.text: He keeps his hand out, smiling. The captain looks petty on TV. Round one to {J}.

choices.label: Say something in his ear
choices.text: Whatever he says, the captain is furious for ninety minutes and gets booked in the 20th minute.

scenarios.title: Rain Delay
scenarios.text: A thunderstorm has stopped the match. Forty minutes in the dressing room, half-time talk long over, nobody knows what to do. Someone has found a football quiz on their phone.

choices.label: Run the quiz
choices.text: He runs a squad quiz. The reserve goalkeeper turns out to know everything. Spirits rise. They win the second half.

choices.label: Stay focused, headphones on
choices.text: He stays in his own bubble, stretching. When play resumes, he's the sharpest man on the pitch.

scenarios.title: Lunch Delivery
scenarios.text: {MUM} has sent lunch to the training ground. For him. And for the entire squad. Twenty-five containers, labelled, with a note telling everyone to eat their vegetables.

choices.label: Share it proudly
choices.text: The squad devours it. The foreign players ask for recipes. The kitchen staff are slightly offended and very impressed.

choices.label: Hide it from the nutritionist
choices.text: The nutritionist finds it anyway, tries some, and asks for the recipe.

scenarios.title: Like Old Times
scenarios.text: {BFf} turns up on his old scooter. 'Get on. Like old times.' The club's insurance would have a heart attack.

choices.label: Get on
choices.text: Helmet, helmet, a ride through the old streets to the old food stall. Nobody recognises him with the helmet on. Bliss.

choices.label: Suggest walking instead
choices.text: They walk. Slower, safer, still wonderful.

scenarios.title: Shopping
scenarios.text: He only wanted a new phone charger. Now there are two hundred people outside the electronics store and the manager is offering him the back exit.

choices.label: Go out the front and sign things
choices.text: He goes out the front and signs for an hour. Two hundred people go home happy. He still doesn't have a charger.

choices.label: Back exit
choices.text: Back exit, quick getaway. The crowd waits another hour, just in case.

scenarios.title: The Manager's Birthday
scenarios.text: It's {M}'s birthday. Nobody has organised anything. The squad is looking at each other.

choices.label: Organise a cake in ten minutes
choices.text: A cake from the canteen, a terrible song, twenty-five grown men. {Mf} pretends to hate it.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.text: Nobody does anything. {Mf} doesn't mention it either.

scenarios.title: The Dog
scenarios.text: A stray dog has wandered onto the training pitch and refuses to leave. It keeps stealing the ball. The session has descended into chaos.

choices.label: Adopt the dog
choices.text: He takes the dog home. It sleeps on his feet that night. The club makes it an honorary mascot.

choices.label: Help the staff find its owner
choices.text: The owner turns up an hour later, mortified. The dog gets a signed ball.

scenarios.title: Number {num}
scenarios.text: A fan writes: their baby was born at 10:{num} pm on the day {J} scored his best goal, so they've named the baby after him. Photo attached.

choices.label: Send the baby a tiny kit
choices.text: A tiny kit with his number on it. The parents frame the delivery note.

choices.label: Reply with a voice message
choices.text: A voice note: 'Welcome to the world, little one.' The parents play it at the christening.

scenarios.title: The Old Ball
scenarios.text: Clearing out his parents' storeroom, he finds it: the ball he played with every day from age six to twelve. Flat, patched, held together with tape and memory.

choices.label: Put it in a glass case
choices.text: It goes in a glass case next to his medals. It's the thing visitors ask about first.

choices.label: Pump it up and play
choices.text: He pumps it up and plays keepy-uppy in the garden while {DAD} watches. Forty-one. {DAD} claps.

scenarios.title: What the Physio Saw
scenarios.text: The physio, wrapping his ankle, says quietly: '{T}'s knee is worse than he's telling anyone. He's hiding it from the manager.'

choices.label: Talk to {T}
choices.text: {T} admits it. He's terrified of losing his place. {J} persuades him to get it treated properly.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.text: He stays out of it. Two weeks later, {T}'s knee gives way in a match.

scenarios.title: The Fridge
scenarios.text: Midnight. The meal plan says no. The fridge says yes: leftover {FOOD}, still in its container, calling his name.

choices.label: Eat it
choices.text: He eats it standing up in the dark. It is magnificent. The scales will know.

choices.label: Close the fridge
choices.text: He closes the fridge. Discipline. He dreams about it.

scenarios.title: Help Me Propose
scenarios.text: A fan has emailed the club: he wants to propose to his girlfriend at Saturday's match, and he wants {J} to hand him the ring on the pitch at half-time.

choices.label: Do it
choices.text: At half-time he walks over with the ring. She says yes. The stadium roars. He's in the wedding photos a year later.

choices.label: Send a video message instead
choices.text: A video message on the big screen. She says yes. Lovely.

scenarios.title: Power Cut
scenarios.text: The whole neighbourhood has lost power. No TV, no phone charge, no internet. Just candles and silence.

choices.label: Go outside and talk to the neighbours
choices.text: Half the street is outside. Someone has a guitar. It's the most social evening he's had in months.

choices.label: Go to bed early
choices.text: Ten hours of sleep. His body thanks the power company.

scenarios.title: The Neighbour's Flag
scenarios.text: His new neighbour has hung a giant flag of {R}, the hated rivals, from the balcony directly opposite his bedroom window.

choices.label: Hang a bigger one
choices.text: He hangs an even bigger flag. The street takes sides. The neighbours become friends through pure competitive pettiness.

choices.label: Invite him for a coffee
choices.text: Over coffee, the neighbour admits he's a closet fan of {J}. The flag stays. So does the friendship.

scenarios.title: Personal Best
scenarios.text: In the gym, he's about to try a lift heavier than ever before. The strength coach is spotting him. Three teammates have stopped to watch.

out.text: Up it goes. The teammates cheer. The coach writes the number on the board.
Something twinges in his back. Nothing serious. Ice and pride.

choices.label: Not today
choices.text: He leaves it for another day. Smart, says the coach.

scenarios.title: Wedding Crashers
scenarios.text: The hotel he's staying in is hosting a wedding. The groom has spotted him in the lobby and is begging him to come in for five minutes. 'My wife will never believe it.'

choices.label: Go in for five minutes
choices.text: Five minutes become forty. He dances with the grandmother. The couple say it was the best moment of their wedding.

choices.label: Send congratulations
choices.text: He signs a napkin: 'Congratulations!' The groom frames it.

scenarios.title: Thirty Letters
scenarios.text: A primary school class has written him thirty letters. Most ask what he eats for breakfast. One asks if he's ever been sad. One says 'my dad says you're rubbish but I like you'.

choices.label: Reply to all thirty
choices.text: Thirty handwritten replies. It takes three evenings. The class pins them to the wall.

choices.label: Send one class letter and a signed ball
choices.text: One letter for the class and a signed ball. The 'rubbish' kid gets the ball.

scenarios.title: {T}'s New Hair
scenarios.text: {T} has arrived at training with a new haircut that can only be described as a mistake. He's asking everyone whether they like it.

choices.label: Tell the truth
choices.text: 'No.' {T} laughs so hard he has to sit down. 'Thank you. Everyone else lied.'

choices.label: Lie kindly
choices.text: 'Looks great, bro.' {T} beams. The squad will be merciless anyway.

scenarios.title: The Taxi Driver
scenarios.text: The taxi driver doesn't recognise him. He talks the whole way about his son, who wants to be a footballer, and how they can't afford boots.

choices.label: Reveal yourself and help
choices.text: At the end of the ride, he hands over a card with his agent's number and money for boots. The driver doesn't understand until he reads the card.

choices.label: Listen and tip well
choices.text: He listens to every word and leaves a generous tip. The driver never knows.

scenarios.title: Birthday Ambush
scenarios.text: Something is wrong. The squad is being too nice. Someone has asked him to step into the shower area 'for a quick photo'.

choices.label: Walk in bravely
choices.text: Ice water, flour, a cake to the face and twenty-five men singing badly. Best birthday in years.

choices.label: Run
choices.text: He runs. They catch him in the car park. Same outcome, more dramatic.

scenarios.title: Fun Run
scenarios.text: A local charity fun run. He's agreed to start it. The organisers now ask if he'd run it too: five kilometres, three thousand participants, one footballer.

choices.label: Run it, at the back
choices.text: He runs at the back with the slowest walkers, chatting the whole way. The photos are lovely.

choices.label: Run it to win
choices.text: He wins by four minutes. A twelve-year-old comes second and is furious.

scenarios.title: 3am Alarm
scenarios.text: The fire alarm in the team hotel goes off at 3am. The whole squad is in the car park in pyjamas. Rival fans are filming from across the road. Kick-off is in twelve hours.

choices.label: Lead a car-park sing-along
choices.text: He starts a song. The squad joins. The rival fans stop filming, confused. Morale, weirdly, is high.

choices.label: Find a quiet corner and doze
choices.text: He sleeps on a bench. Survival.

scenarios.title: The Tutor
scenarios.text: His language tutor has set homework: describe your family in five sentences. He's been staring at the page for twenty minutes, thinking about home.

choices.label: Write about them honestly
choices.text: Five sentences become two pages. The tutor reads it and gently corrects nothing. 'Send this to your mother.'

choices.label: Call home instead
choices.text: He calls home and forgets about the homework. The tutor understands.

scenarios.title: The Rookie's Question
scenarios.text: A seventeen-year-old just up from the academy sits next to him at lunch and asks, very quietly, 'How do you deal with it when the crowd boos you?'

choices.label: Tell him the truth
choices.text: 'You remember it's not personal, and you go home to people who love you.' The kid nods like it's scripture.

choices.label: Make him laugh
choices.text: 'You pretend they're singing.' The kid laughs. It helps more than he expected.

scenarios.title: Splash
scenarios.text: His phone has fallen into the toilet two hours before kick-off. It contains his pre-match playlist, his lucky photos and three unanswered messages from {MUM}.

choices.label: Rice and prayer
choices.text: Bowl of rice, a prayer, a teammate's phone for the playlist. Somehow, the phone survives.

choices.label: Embrace phone-free matchday
choices.text: No phone all day. He's calmer than ever. Maybe this is the secret.

scenarios.title: The Barber
scenarios.text: His barber has opinions on everything: the manager's tactics, the president's car, the price of fuel, and whether {J} should play further forward. He is often right.

choices.label: Listen to his tactical advice
choices.text: The barber draws a formation on a napkin with hair gel. It's not bad, actually.

choices.label: Ask him about life instead
choices.text: The barber talks about his late wife and his three daughters. {J} leaves with a haircut and a full heart.

scenarios.title: For Sale
scenarios.text: His very first professional shirt, signed and given to a fan years ago, is for sale online. The seller's listing says: 'Need money for medical bills.'

choices.label: Buy it, and send the money anyway
choices.text: He buys it at full price and sends the seller extra for the bills. The seller sends a long, emotional thank-you.

choices.label: Let it sell to someone else
choices.text: It sells. He hopes the bills got paid.

scenarios.title: Gridlock
scenarios.text: Stuck in traffic on the way to the stadium. Fans in the cars around him have spotted him. Someone is passing a shirt through a window to be signed.

choices.label: Sign everything passed to you
choices.text: Windows down, shirts going car to car. A traffic jam becomes a party.

choices.label: Windows up, focus
choices.text: Windows up, headphones on. Matchday mode.

scenarios.title: Is This Allowed?
scenarios.text: He has a terrible cold. The pharmacist hands him a strong medicine. He suddenly remembers the anti-doping talk.

choices.label: Call the club doctor before taking it
choices.text: The doctor says no: banned ingredient. He gets a safe alternative. Close call.

choices.label: Just tea and honey
choices.text: Tea, honey, sleep. The cold lasts a day longer. His career stays safe.

scenarios.title: Dance With Me
scenarios.text: {Pf} puts on a song from when they first met and holds out her hand in the middle of the kitchen.

choices.label: Dance
choices.text: They dance badly in the kitchen until the song ends, then play it again.

choices.label: 'My legs are dead'
choices.text: She laughs and dances by herself. He watches. It's still lovely.

scenarios.title: After Prayers
scenarios.text: After Friday prayers, an old man stops him: 'I prayed for your knee last month. Did it work?' Half the congregation is waiting for the answer.

choices.label: 'It did. Thank you.'
choices.text: The old man is delighted and promises to keep praying, especially before derbies.

choices.label: Stay and talk with the community
choices.text: He stays for an hour, drinking tea, hearing stories. He feels at home for the first time in weeks.

scenarios.title: Cook-Along
scenarios.text: Fans keep asking what he cooks. He's never cooked on camera. {SIB} dares him to do a live cooking stream.

out.text: He burns the rice and forgets the salt. A hundred thousand people watch. It's the most charming thing he's ever done.
The smoke alarm goes off live. The clip is everywhere.

choices.label: No way
choices.text: He refuses. {SIB} calls him a coward. He is a coward, about cooking.

scenarios.title: The Wrong Bus
scenarios.text: He's got on the wrong team bus: the women's team's bus, heading to a different stadium. The women are delighted. The driver is not.

choices.label: Laugh and enjoy the ride
choices.text: They drop him off with a lot of jokes. He's on the club's social media as the 'newest women's team signing'.

choices.label: Panic
choices.text: He panics. They laugh. A taxi gets him to the right place just in time.

scenarios.title: Face to Face
scenarios.text: At a restaurant, the pundit who has criticised him on TV all season is at the next table. He's noticed {J}. The silence is very loud.

choices.label: Go over and shake his hand
choices.text: He goes over, shakes his hand and says, 'Keep watching.' The pundit is speechless. His next segment is noticeably kinder.

choices.label: Send him a dessert
choices.text: A dessert arrives at the pundit's table with a note: 'From your favourite player.' He laughs despite himself.

scenarios.title: A Video Call
scenarios.text: A children's hospital asks if he'd video-call a boy who's very ill and talks about {J} constantly. Fifteen minutes. The boy doesn't know.

choices.label: Call him, for as long as he wants
choices.text: The call lasts an hour. They talk about football, dogs and dinosaurs. The boy's mother sends a message afterwards he'll keep forever.

choices.label: Call, then send a care package
choices.text: A call and a box of signed things. The boy sleeps with the ball.

scenarios.title: Test Drive
scenarios.text: A car dealership has invited him to test-drive a supercar. The salesman keeps saying 'no obligation' in a way that clearly means 'please buy this'.

choices.label: Drive it and walk away
choices.text: Ten minutes of absurd speed, then he hands back the keys. The salesman's face falls. His savings don't.

choices.label: Drive it to {MUM}'s house to show her
choices.text: He drives it to {MUM}'s. She asks what it costs and then makes him sit through a lecture. Worth it.

scenarios.title: Flooded Streets
scenarios.text: Heavy rain has flooded part of his old neighbourhood. Neighbours are moving furniture out of houses. He has a free morning.

choices.label: Grab a shovel and help
choices.text: Four hours of mud, furniture and sandbags. Nobody takes photos until the end, and then everybody does.

choices.label: Pay for emergency supplies
choices.text: He pays for food, water and cleaning supplies for the whole street.

scenarios.title: The Cabinet
scenarios.text: {MUM} has built a trophy cabinet in the living room. It currently holds his medals, a photo of his first goal and, for some reason, a ceramic cat.

choices.label: Ask about the cat
choices.text: The cat, apparently, was in the room when he scored his first goal on TV. It is now part of history.

choices.label: Add something new
choices.text: He adds his first boots. {MUM} rearranges everything around them for an hour.

scenarios.title: Arrival
scenarios.text: As the team bus pulls up to the stadium, thousands of fans line the road, flares, scarves, singing. Someone has made a banner with his face on it.

choices.label: Stand at the window and salute them
choices.text: He stands at the window with his fist on his heart. The roar shakes the bus.

choices.label: Film it for {MUM}
choices.text: He films it. {MUM} watches it twenty times and shows the neighbours.

scenarios.title: The Old Video
scenarios.text: A former youth coach sends him a video of his first academy match, age twelve: tiny, fast, terrible at defending, and celebrating a goal like he'd won the World Cup.

choices.label: Watch it with the squad
choices.text: The squad watches it on the big screen. They cheer the twelve-year-old's goal louder than anything all season.

choices.label: Send it to your family
choices.text: {DAD} watches it and calls him, voice thick. 'I remember that day.'

scenarios.title: The Queue
scenarios.text: A long queue outside a popular restaurant. The manager spots him and offers to take him straight in, past forty people who've been waiting an hour.

choices.label: Wait like everyone else
choices.text: He waits. Somebody films it. 'Humble king,' says the internet.

choices.label: Accept and go in
choices.text: He goes in. Some of the queue grumbles. One person films that, too.

scenarios.title: Sunday Lunch With Her Parents
scenarios.text: {Pf}'s father has been talking for forty minutes about a match from 1989. {Pf} is mouthing 'sorry' across the table.

choices.label: Ask follow-up questions
choices.text: He asks about the match. The father's face lights up. Forty more minutes. {Pf} loves him for it.

choices.label: Change the subject gently
choices.text: He steers it to the father's garden. Also a long story, but a better one.

scenarios.title: Translate for Me?
scenarios.text: {T}, the new signing, can't make himself understood at the bank. He's called {J}, of all people, to help translate a mortgage form.

choices.label: Go to the bank with him
choices.text: Two hours at the bank, one mortgage, a new friendship.

choices.label: Send the club's translator
choices.text: The translator handles it. {T} is grateful, if a bit lonely.

scenarios.title: The Old Flatmate
scenarios.text: His first flatmate from the academy, who didn't make it, messages out of nowhere: he's working in a warehouse now, has a daughter, and just wanted to say he's proud.

choices.label: Meet him for dinner
choices.text: They meet and laugh about the old flat, the burnt rice, the coach who hated them both. A friendship rekindled.

choices.label: Send something for his daughter
choices.text: A signed shirt and a toy for the daughter. The flatmate sends back a photo of her wearing it as a dress.

scenarios.title: Sleepwalking
scenarios.text: He wakes up in the corridor of the team hotel in his underwear, holding a pillow, with the assistant manager staring at him.

choices.label: Say nothing and walk back
choices.text: He walks back with great dignity. At breakfast, the assistant manager says nothing. His eyes say everything.

choices.label: Explain everything
choices.text: He explains. The assistant manager nods slowly and tells the whole squad by lunch.

scenarios.title: A Boy Selling Snacks
scenarios.text: At a traffic light, a boy selling snacks knocks on his window. He recognises {J} and forgets to sell anything; he just wants to talk about the last match.

choices.label: Buy everything he's carrying
choices.text: He buys the whole tray and tells the boy to go home early. The boy runs off grinning.

choices.label: Talk until the light changes
choices.text: They talk football for one red light. The boy waves until the car is out of sight.

scenarios.title: Film Night
scenarios.text: The squad is having a film night at the training ground. The argument about which film is now in its second hour.

choices.label: Pick a film nobody will agree with
choices.text: He picks a cartoon about a talking fish. Twenty-five grown men cry at the ending.

choices.label: Suggest a documentary about a football legend
choices.text: The documentary about an old legend fires everyone up. Training the next day is ferocious.
